key_big: Multiplication means equal groups: 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3.
body_html:
Multiplication is equal groups

4 × 3 means 4 groups of 3. Add 3 four times: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12.

An array has rows that are all the same. 3 rows of 5 dots is 3 × 5 = 15. Turn it round and it is 5 × 3. The answer is still 15.

Skip count to find a fact

Count in jumps of the same size. Count the jumps, not the numbers.

Missing factors

In 5 × ? = 30, count in 5s until you reach 30. Count how many fives you said.

Example

5 × ? = 30

5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 fives.

Answer: 6

Word problems: draw a model

Draw equal units. Many units: multiply. One unit: share or divide.

Equal groups

A car has 4 wheels. How many wheels do 7 cars have?

7 groups of 4: 7 × 4 = 28.

Answer: 28 wheels

faq.q: Which multiplication tables are taught in Primary 2 in Singapore?
faq.a: Primary 2 students learn the multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10. The tables of 6, 7, 8 and 9 come in Primary 3.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn the tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10?
faq.a: Start with equal groups of real objects, then skip count: 2, 4, 6 or 5, 10, 15. Use tips such as “4 is double 2” and “× 10 puts a 0 at the end”.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in P2 multiplication?
faq.a: Adding instead of multiplying, for example 3 groups of 5 = 8. Another is counting one jump too many when skip counting.

faq.q: Are the tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics syllabus has the multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 in Primary 2, with multiplying and dividing within these tables and simple word problems.

items.e: There are 3 groups of 4. 3 × 4 = 12. 4 is double 2. 3 × 2 = 6. Double it: 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 5 groups of 2. 5 × 2 = 10. 5 × 2 is double 5: 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 5. 4 × 5 = 20. Count in 5s 4 times: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups of 10. 2 × 10 = 20. 2 tens make 20. 2 × 10 = 20.

items.q: How many dots are there?
items.e: There are 3 rows of 5. 3 × 5 = 15. Count in 5s 3 times: 5, 10, 15. So 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: How many dots are there?
items.e: There are 4 rows of 3. 4 × 3 = 12. Count in 3s 4 times: 3, 6, 9, 12. So 4 × 3 = 12.

items.e: There are 5 rows of 4. 5 × 4 = 20. 4 is double 2. 5 × 2 = 10. Double it: 10 + 10 = 20.

items.q: Which multiplication matches the picture?
items.e: There are 4 groups of 3: 4 × 3 = 12. 4 + 3 only adds the two numbers.

items.q: Which multiplication matches the picture?
items.e: There are 2 rows of 5: 2 × 5 = 10. 2 + 5 only adds the two numbers.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the boxes. There are 5 groups. 3 is the number in each group. 15 is the total.

items.q: How many counters are in each group?
items.e: Each box has 5 counters. 3 is the number of groups. 15 is the total.

items.q: 8 counters are put in groups of 2. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the boxes: 4 groups of 2. Check: 4 × 2 = 8.

items.q: Which multiplication is the same as 4 + 4 + 4?
items.e: There are three 4s. 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: Which multiplication is the same as 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?
items.e: Count the 5s. There are six 5s, so it is 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 5 groups of 2?
items.e: 5 groups of 2 means five 2s: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.

items.q: What is 3 groups of 10?
items.e: 3 groups of 10 is 3 tens: 3 × 10 = 30. 13 adds 3 and 10.

items.q: 2 × 5 = 5 × ?
items.e: You can turn the array round. 2 rows of 5 is the same as 5 rows of 2. So ? = 2.

items.q: Kavya says 3 groups of 5 is 8. What did she do wrong?
c: She counted one group too many
items.e: 3 + 5 = 8, so she added. 3 groups of 5 is 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: There are 4 bags. Each bag has 2 apples. Which multiplication shows this?
items.e: 4 bags is 4 groups. Each group has 2. So it is 4 × 2 = 8.

items.q: An array has 3 rows. There are 18 dots. How many dots are in each row?
items.e: 3 × ? = 18. Count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. That is 6 threes, so there are 6 dots in each row.

items.q: Which multiplication does this number line show?
items.e: Count the jumps, not the numbers. There are 6 jumps of 2 from 0 to 12. So 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: Which multiplication does this number line show?

items.q: Which multiplication does this number line show?
items.e: Count the jumps, not the numbers. There are 5 jumps of 10 from 0 to 50. So 5 × 10 = 50.

items.q: Jun Jie counts in 5s to find 4 × 5. He says: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. What is 4 × 5?
items.e: 4 × 5 needs only 4 fives: 5, 10, 15, 20. He counted one 5 too many. 4 × 5 = 20.
Count in 5s 3 times: 5, 10, 15. So 3 × 5 = 15.

items.q: 2 × 6 = 12. Double it to find 4 × 6.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 6 is double 2 × 6: 12 + 12 = 24.

items.q: 2 × 8 = 16. Double it to find 4 × 8.
items.e: 4 is double 2, so 4 × 8 is double 2 × 8: 16 + 16 = 32.
Count in 3s 4 times: 3, 6, 9, 12. So 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: Which number is in the multiplication table of 3?
Which number is not in the multiplication table of 4?
items.e: The table of 4 goes 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40. 30 is not in the list.
You can multiply in any order. 8 × 3 = 3 × 8 = 24. 11 adds the numbers.
Count in 2s to 14: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 7 twos. So ? = 7. Check: 2 × 7 = 14.
Count in 10s to 60: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 tens. So ? = 6. Check: 10 × 6 = 60.
Count in 4s to 28: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28. That is 7 fours. So ? = 7. Check: 4 × 7 = 28.
Count in 3s to 18: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. That is 6 threes. So ? = 6. Check: 3 × 6 = 18.
Count in 4s to 32: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32. That is 8 fours. So ? = 8. Check: 4 × 8 = 32.
Count in 2s to 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 twos. So ? = 6. Check: 6 × 2 = 12.
Count in 10s to 40: 10, 20, 30, 40. That is 4 tens. So ? = 4. Check: 4 × 10 = 40.
Count in 3s to 24: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24. That is 8 threes. So ? = 8. Check: 8 × 3 = 24.
Count in 2s to 16: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. That is 8 twos. So ? = 8. Check: 8 × 2 = 16.

items.q: 4 × ? = 28. How many jumps of 4 make 28?
items.e: Count the jumps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28. There are 7 jumps. 8 counts the 0 as well.

items.q: ? × 10 = 30. How many groups of 10 are there?
items.e: Count the boxes: 3 groups of 10. 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q: Mei Ling says the missing number in 5 × ? = 35 is 30. What is the correct number?
items.e: 35 − 5 = 30 takes away instead of counting groups. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. That is 7 fives.
Count the 3s. There are four 3s, so ? = 4.
You can multiply in any order. 7 × 10 = 10 × 7, so ? = 7.
2 × 6 = 12. 4 × 3 = 12, so ? = 3. 12 is the product, not the missing number.

items.q: Mdm Wong puts 4 curry puffs on each plate. There are 5 plates. How many curry puffs are there?
items.e: 5 plates of 4: 5 × 4 = 20. 9 is 5 + 4. It adds instead of multiplies.

items.q: A bicycle has 2 wheels. There are 8 bicycles at the void deck. How many wheels are there?
items.e: 8 bicycles of 2 wheels: 8 × 2 = 16. 10 is 8 + 2.

items.q: A tricycle has 3 wheels. How many wheels do 6 tricycles have?
A car has 4 wheels. There are 7 cars in the car park. How many wheels are there?
items.e: 7 units of 4: 7 × 4 = 28. 24 is only 6 cars.

items.q: There are 10 sweets in each packet. How many sweets are there in 9 packets?
A bowl of laksa costs $5. Sarah buys 4 bowls for her family. How much does she pay?
Raju saves $2 every day. How much does he save in 9 days?
A sweet costs 10¢. Chloe buys 6 sweets. How much does she pay?
There are 3 plates. Each plate has 4 slices of kaya toast. How many slices are there altogether?
items.e: 3 groups of 4: 3 × 4 = 12. 3 is the number of plates, and 4 is the number on one plate.

items.q: A packet of stickers costs 5¢. Xin Yi buys 8 packets. How much does she pay?
For National Day, the class makes 6 rows of flags. There are 5 flags in each row. How many flags are there?
items.e: 6 units of 5: 6 × 5 = 30. 25 is only 5 rows.

items.q: Mrs Lim shares 20 stickers equally among 5 pupils. How many stickers does each pupil get?
Mr Tan puts 24 mandarin oranges into bags. He puts 4 oranges in each bag. How many bags does he use?
items.e: Count in 4s to 24: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. That is 6 fours. Check: 6 × 4 = 24.

items.q: 30 pupils stand in rows of 10 at assembly. How many rows are there?
items.e: 30 is 3 tens. 3 × 10 = 30, so there are 3 rows.

items.q: Hafiz has $16. He spends $2 each day at recess. How many days will the money last?
items.e: Count in 2s to 16: that is 8 twos. 8 × $2 = $16, so it lasts 8 days.

items.q: Mr Rahman cuts a rope 35 m long into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 5 units = 35 m. 1 unit = 35 ÷ 5 = 7 m. Check: 5 × 7 = 35.

items.q: 27 pupils visit the Singapore Zoo. They walk in groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count in 3s to 27: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27. That is 9 threes. Check: 9 × 3 = 27.

items.q: A teacher puts 32 pencils equally into 4 cups. How many pencils are in each cup?
Zhi Hao buys 3 packets of stickers. There are 5 stickers in each packet. He gives away 4 stickers. How many stickers does he have left?
items.e: 3 × 5 = 15. Then 15 − 4 = 11. 15 forgets the 4 stickers given away.

items.q: Priya has 4 boxes of crayons with 10 crayons in each box. She also has 3 loose crayons. How many crayons does she have altogether?
items.e: 4 × 10 = 40. Then 40 + 3 = 43. 40 forgets the 3 loose crayons.
